html_en:
A big day for AI memory, agent infrastructure, and one very fast chip — the industry's plumbing is getting a serious upgrade, even as cracks appear in the foundations.

🧠 Memory Gets Serious

The most coordinated theme of the day: AI assistants are finally getting persistent, coherent memory — and both Anthropic and OpenAI are racing to make it feel seamless.

Claude announced unified memory across its chat and Cowork surfaces:

"Hand Cowork a task and it starts from what Claude already knows from your chats: the project you talked through, your manager's preferences, or the client from last quarter." — @claudeai

The implementation is notably transparent — everything Claude remembers is saved as an editable list in Settings, and sensitive topics like health or religion stay out of memory by default unless you opt in. Cat Wu, who shipped the feature, invited further feedback. Meanwhile, on the ChatGPT side, Boris Cherny was characteristically understated: "A small improvement: memory is now simpler and more powerful. Enjoy!" — a tweet that earned 1,400+ likes, suggesting people had been waiting for exactly this.

Garry Tan captured the broader zeitgeist with his characteristically pithy take: "You need to be cross-harness memory maxxing."

🛠️ The Codex Ecosystem Expands — With Caveats

OpenAI's Codex is clearly having a moment, with a new team plan and Dev Day anticipation running hot. Thomas Sottiaux laid out the new offering: Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, and Microsoft 365 integrations, SAML/SSO, centralized billing, and crucially — no five-hour limits. "So much demand for this one," he noted, understating things considerably given the 2,900 likes.

But not everyone is celebrating. Shawn Wang (@swyx) issued a pointed warning:

"PSA: do not use codex 'locked use' capabilities right now. it is currently relying on unstable mac features and has completely locked me out of my macos keychain twice this week." — @swyx

He noted that Apple's developer forums acknowledge this as a "known bug." The tension he identifies — cloud isn't ready, but local is broken — is a real growing pain for anyone trying to use these agent tools in production.

On a more encouraging note, @trq212 teased that Claude Code is about to get more hackable: "excited to share more on how we're making Claude Code more hackable soon."

⚡ Sam's Chip, and the Infrastructure Arms Race

The most retweeted moment of the day came in six words. Sam Altman on OpenAI's new silicon:

"we made a chip and it is fast" — @sama

32,000 likes and counting. No further elaboration required, apparently.

The chip announcement sits alongside serious developer tooling news from Vercel. Guillermo Rauch shipped two things worth bookmarking: Run SDK, a lightweight QuickJS secure sandbox for agent-generated code ("faster and more cost-efficient" than full sandboxes), and Vercel Connect going GA, which he described as addressing "the hardest problem in building agents": secure connectivity to services and data. Run vercel connect create notion, get an MCP client you can query on behalf of an authenticated user. Elegant.

🌐 Reinventing Search for the Agentic Web

The most intellectually substantive content of the day came from the Training Data podcast, where former Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal laid out his thesis for Parallel Web Systems — a startup rebuilding search infrastructure from scratch for AI agents.

His core provocation:

"Our view at Parallel is that human click data is a bug. An agent doing work with search should rely on agent feedback, not human feedback." — Parag Agrawal

The argument is compelling: the two main moats Google built — proprietary click data at scale and the cost of crawling the full web — are both eroding. LLMs can generate high-quality relevance ratings cheaply; and agents, unlike humans, will tolerate latency in exchange for depth, meaning you can crawl on-demand rather than preindex everything. Parallel launched a search agent first, not a search product, precisely because "if you're doing deep research, you have patience to the extent of a minute."

Watch/Listen: Parallel's Parag Agrawal: Building a New Web for AI Agents — Training Data Podcast

🩺 AI as Advocate: The Human Angle

Amid all the infrastructure news, one of the day's most moving contributions came from Peter Yang, who open-sourced /fuck-cancer — an AI skill built to help patients and caregivers navigate cancer diagnosis.

"The volume of doctors, documents, and insurance paperwork can quickly become overwhelming." — a caregiver, quoted by @petergyang

The skill creates a living brief: care-team contacts, next actions (limited to three), confirmed facts versus unknowns, plain-English medical glossary, and a running care log. It pulls from the National Cancer Institute and ClinicalTrials.gov. Yang built it while supporting his mother. It's available free on GitHub and works with both ChatGPT/Codex and Claude Code. This is what Aditya Agarwal was gesturing at when he argued that AI's public perception problem will only shift "when AI is able to find cures for diseases that ail everyone." Tools like this won't cure cancer — but they might help someone fight it more effectively.
html_zh:
今天的科技圈，AI的记忆力突然变得无处不在——Claude打通了跨平台记忆，OpenAI悄悄发布了芯片，而前Twitter CEO则在悄然重构整个互联网的底层逻辑。

🧠 记忆大战：Claude率先打通跨平台上下文

如果说AI助手最令人沮丧的地方是什么，大概就是每次换个界面就像跟一个失忆的陌生人重新认识。Anthropic今天正面回应了这个痛点。

"Claude现在在Chat和Claude Cowork之间共享同一套记忆，由你决定里面存什么。把任务交给Cowork，它会从Claude已经知道的内容出发——你上次讨论的项目、你经理的偏好、上个季度的客户。"
— @claudeai

Claude团队成员 @_catwu 也补充说，这次更新是"根据用户反馈"做出的调整，现在只需告诉Claude记住某件事一次，它就能跨界面保留这个上下文。与此同时，@bcherny 也简短地宣布记忆功能"更简单、更强大"。

当然，隐私是不可回避的问题。Anthropic特别说明，健康状况、宗教信仰等敏感话题默认不纳入记忆，需要用户主动在设置中开启。Garry Tan 则用一句话点出了这场记忆军备竞赛的本质：

"你需要跨平台全力记忆。"
— @garrytan

⚡ OpenAI自研芯片登场，Sam Altman用最少的字说了最大的事

今天互联网上转发量最高的一条推文，只有七个英文单词：

"We made a chip and it is fast."
— @sama（32,000+ 点赞）

OpenAI Dev Day即将到来，@petergyang 等开发者已经迫不及待地表示将亲赴现场。与此同时，OpenAI团队成员 @thsottiaux 也透露了备受期待的ChatGPT团队版计划的细节，涵盖Google Workspace、Slack、GitHub等全套集成，支持SAML/SSO/MFA，并去掉了每日5小时的使用限制。用他自己的话说：

"好产品需要时间打磨。至少34天。"
— @thsottiaux

🕸️ 为AI代理重建互联网：前Twitter CEO的新赌注

如果说记忆是AI助手的软件层，那搜索就是整个代理网络的基础设施。前Twitter CEO Parag Agrawal 创立的 Parallel Web Systems 正在做一件听起来疯狂、但逻辑严密的事：为AI代理重新发明搜索引擎。

在 Training Data 播客中，他解释了为什么传统搜索对代理来说是错的：

"我们在Parallel的观点是，人类点击数据是一个缺陷。代理在搜索中工作，应该依赖代理反馈，而不是人类反馈。"
— Parag Agrawal，Watch/Listen: Training Data podcast

他的核心论点是：代理使用搜索的频率将是人类的一千倍，因此整个索引、爬取和排名的逻辑都需要重建。Parallel没有一开始就建造全量索引（那需要天文数字的资金），而是先推出了一个搜索代理产品——允许在查询到达后实时爬取网页，用户愿意等待几分钟来换取更深度的研究结果。这是一个以时间换基础设施的聪明走法。

Box CEO Aaron Levie 今天也呼应了同一个主题：

"世界不只想要原始模型和代理；它想要问题被解决、结果被实现。溢价将属于那些能够将智能扩散到文明每个角落的公司——将原始token转化为现实世界成果。"

🛠️ 开发者工具：从癌症导航到El Niño监测

这一周，"用AI做有意义的事"这个主题格外突出。@petergyang 开源了一个名为 /fuck-cancer 的AI技能，专门帮助癌症患者和家属在就医过程中整理信息、与医疗系统周旋。

"我建立这个技能是为了解决这些问题：它创建并更新一份实用简报，包含五个部分——患者与护理团队信息、接下来要做的三件具体事情、已知事实与未知事项的分离、用通俗英语解释的医学术语，以及最近更新的护理日志。"
— @petergyang

另一边，@nikunj 用ChatGPT Codex和Railway搭建了一个El Niño实时监测站（elneenyo.com），数据直接来自政府来源。小工具，真需求。

在基础设施层，Vercel CEO @rauchg 连发两条重磅公告：Vercel Connect 正式上线，一行命令即可为代理创建连接Notion等服务的MCP客户端；同时推出 Run SDK，在轻量级QuickJS沙箱中安全执行代理写的代码，"更快、成本更低"。

不过，也有人踩了坑。@swyx 发出公开警告：不要使用Codex的"锁定使用"功能——这个功能依赖不稳定的macOS特性，本周已经让他的macOS钥匙串崩溃两次。"云端方案还没到位，但本地方案也还没稳定。"这大概是当前AI工具链的真实写照。

📐 评估体系需要一份路线图

最后，留给所有在生产环境中部署AI的团队一个值得收藏的洞察。@realmadhuguru 在其评估系列第9篇中提出了"评估路线图问题"：

"大多数评估体系失败，是因为团队把它们当作静态文物，而用户的期望和行为已经进化。你的评估需要一份随产品和实际使用模式共同演进的路线图。"
— @realmadhuguru

他用一个金融研究代理的例子说明：用户第一周问"总结这份5页财报"，两个月后就变成了"监控我的投资组合，当有重大变化时提醒我"。如果你的评估体系还停留在第一周，流失率会告诉你答案。完整的九篇系列值得一读。
